visual_findings: All eight six-page contact sheets were actually observed separately, then all11 selected detailed pages. Rendering alone received no reading credit.

Pages448-449 distinguish Hamilton rule c<rb as an evolvability condition from a psychological or moral decision rule; page467 Box8.1 explicitly reports two experiments refuting a specific kin-infidelity prediction.

Figure8.1/page463 has tendency-to-help scores on a displayed1.4to2.6axis, not probabilities. The first age label visually reads >1Yr while prose page462 says one-year-olds; primary coding and intended inequality remain unverified. Everyday and hypothetical emergency age patterns differ.

Figure8.2/page476 shows four dimensions: Closeness,Time,Knowledge,Resources, with four grandparent categories and a More/Less axis. The Knowledge bar for mothers father is slightly above mothers mother; do not convert an overall tendency into highest on every dimension. The cited figure source is a1995conference presentation.

Figure8.3/page482 shows willingness-to-help scores for four cousin-line categories, a displayed5to6.4truncated vertical axis and error bars; not actual rescue rates or percentages. Figure8.4/page488 is a schematic of three kinds of family conflict, not measured prevalence.

Box8.2/pages480-482 is aunts/uncles/cousins text with Figure8.3. Selected pages477,479,487 preserve alternative explanations, a nonreplication and critique of extending family-formation models to humans. Photo473 is illustrative.

Figure9.1/page507 is the payoff matrix for playerA: R3,S0,T5,P1 with A rows and B columns; adjacent506states T>R>P>S and R>(S+T)/2. A tournament result in that strategy set is not universal optimality or a chat punishment rule.

Unnumbered Wason cards/page517 are a,b,2,3; to test vowel implies even, a and3 are relevant. Unnumbered altruist-detection cards/page522 are helps,does-not-help,does-not-seek-credit,seeks-credit; the printed rule is helps implies seeks-credit. Page520 is an illustrative drinking-rule photograph and caption, not another card diagram or current legal guidance.
Figure9.2/page529 displays offer percentages by perceived cost category1to7, cost rated by independent raters, comparing Public and Anonymous conditions; cost is not volunteer hours or money.

Figure9.3 and9.4 share page539 but are separate images: benefit ratings versus reported frequency, with SSF/OSF labels and1997conference-source captions. Neither graph proves mutual interest, consent, or a percentage of real friends seeking sex.
Figure9.5/page545 is average1to7ratings, with error bars and four dimensions. Punishers score higher in three displayed dimensions, not in Nice; the graph does not license interpersonal retaliation.

Page527 lists five altruism routes including need-based transfers, whereas the four-item list in summary549omits that route after discussing it. Page533 states no empirical effectiveness tests for the listed irreplaceability strategies at the time of the text; no claim is made about research status in2026.
